name: Screen supplier invoices for duplicates and PO mismatches with Gmail, Sheets and AI

parameters.content:
## Screen supplier invoices for duplicates and PO mismatches with Gmail, Sheets and AI

### How it works

1. Gmail hands over every email carrying a PDF, and each attachment becomes its own invoice.
2. An LLM reads the PDF and returns eleven named fields, copied rather than inferred.
3. The invoice is checked against itself: net plus tax, the dates, and the IBAN check digits.
4. It is checked against the ledger for a bill already paid — same supplier and amount under a new number, not only the same number twice.
5. The bank account is compared with the supplier master file, because changing it is how invoice fraud is done.
6. What survives is matched to a purchase order and to what was received, then cleared, held, or sent to a named approver.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect Gmail, Google Sheets and OpenAI credentials.
- [ ] Create a sheet with three tabs: Suppliers, Purchase orders, Ledger.
- [ ] Put the sheet ID, both approver addresses and your limits in Set Workflow Parameters.
- [ ] Set the same sheet ID on Read Ledger Data from Sheets, which runs on its own trigger.
- [ ] Run it on one real invoice before switching it on.

### Customization

Every threshold lives in Set Workflow Parameters. The checks themselves are two Code nodes: add one to the same risk list and the routing, the emails and the ledger carry it without another edit.

## Receive the invoice and settings

Gmail hands over every message carrying a PDF. **Set Workflow Parameters** is the only node you have to edit, and it runs once per batch of mail rather than once per email, which is what stops the three reads below from repeating.

## Load the three registers once

Who the suppliers are, what is on order, and what has already been through here. Each **Aggregate** node folds a read down to one item on purpose: a Sheets node runs once per item it receives, so without them the next read would repeat for every row.

## Split and loop each invoice

One email can carry two invoices and a signature image. Each PDF becomes its own item, and they go through one by one so an approval waiting three days cannot hold up the next invoice.

## Read the PDF and extract fields

Text out of the PDF, then eleven named fields out of the text. The model is told to copy rather than infer and to return a blank instead of a guess, because a blank stops here and a guess gets paid.

options.systemPromptTemplate:
You are reading a supplier invoice for an accounts-payable team.

Copy what is printed. Never infer, never calculate, never tidy up.
If a field is genuinely not on the page, return an empty string, or 0 for a number — a blank is handled downstream, an invented value is paid.

Amounts must be plain numbers with no currency symbol and no thousands separator. Dates must be copied exactly as they appear, in the invoice's own format; something else works out what they mean.

attributes.name: supplier_name
attributes.description: The company that issued the invoice — the seller, not the customer being billed. Exactly as printed.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The invoice number or reference, exactly as printed, including any letters or slashes.

attributes.name: invoice_date
attributes.description: The date the invoice was issued, copied exactly as printed. Do not reformat it.

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The payment due date exactly as printed. Empty string if the invoice does not state one.

attributes.name: po_number
attributes.description: The customer's purchase order or PO number quoted on the invoice. Empty string if none is quoted.

attributes.name: currency
attributes.description: ISO 4217 code such as EUR, GBP, USD. Infer it from the currency symbol if no code is printed.

attributes.name: net_amount
attributes.description: The total before tax, as a plain number. 0 if only a gross total is printed.

attributes.name: tax_amount
attributes.description: The total VAT or sales tax, as a plain number. 0 if none is shown.

attributes.name: total_amount
attributes.description: The final amount payable including tax, as a plain number. No currency symbol, no thousands separator.

attributes.name: iban
attributes.description: The IBAN or bank account the invoice asks to be paid into. Copy every character. Empty string if absent.

attributes.name: line_item_count
attributes.description: How many separate lines are itemised on the invoice.

parameters.content:
## Check the invoice against itself

Net plus tax against the total, a due date that is not before the invoice date, a VAT rate that exists, and the IBAN against its own check digits. Amounts and dates are read both ways round, since 1.234,56 and 03/04 mean two things.

## Match against orders and past payments

The node this template exists for. Three questions: have we paid this already, is the bank account the one we used last time, and was it ordered and received. Every finding lands in one list with a severity, and the routing reads that list.

## Route the invoice by outcome

Held, sent to a person, or straight through. Straight through needs all four: nothing blocking, nothing to review, a purchase order it matched, and a total under the auto-approval limit.

## Hold it and tell finance

A duplicate, a changed bank account, more billed than ordered or than received. Nobody is asked to approve it, because approval is not the question yet.

parameters.subject: =HELD: {{ $json.supplier_name }} {{ $json.invoice_number }} - {{ $json.risk_codes }}

parameters.content:
## Send it to a named approver

The findings go out with the invoice and the workflow waits up to three days for the answer. Who is asked depends on the amount: the AP manager under your manager limit, the finance director above it.

parameters.subject: =Approve? {{ $json.supplier_name }} {{ $json.currency }} {{ $json.total_amount }} ({{ $json.invoice_number }})

parameters.content:
## Clear small clean invoices to pay

Under the limit, matched to an order, nothing flagged. No email to anybody: an approval request nobody needed to read is how people stop reading the ones that matter.

## Send unreadable invoices to AP

A scan of a scan, a photograph, a language the extraction did not expect. It is not guessed at and not dropped — it goes to a person, and it is still recorded.

parameters.subject: =Unreadable invoice from {{ $json.sender }}

parameters.content:
## Write the outcome to the ledger

All four branches end here. One row per invoice, matched on supplier and invoice number so a second run updates the row instead of adding one. That row is what the duplicate check reads next time, and what the morning sweep works from.

## Sweep the ledger every weekday

The second entry point, and the one that makes the first worth having. It finds what the invoice-by-invoice pass cannot see: approvals nobody answered, holds nobody resolved, invoices falling due, and pairs of rows that look like one bill twice.

## Send the morning list

One email, and only when there is something in it. A report that arrives every day whether or not anything is wrong stops being read by the third week.

parameters.subject: =Accounts payable: {{ $json.count }} thing(s) open

parameters.content:
## Report a failure of the workflow

A third entry point that fires only when a production run errors — a Sheets quota, an OpenAI timeout, a malformed PDF. Without it a failure is silent, and a silent accounts-payable workflow looks exactly like a quiet week.

parameters.subject: =Invoice workflow failed: {{ $json.execution.id }}
